chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim from Ali from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who divorced his wife, can he marry her sister? He said, 'No, until her waiting period (iddah) expires.'
He said, And I asked him about a man who had a wife and she died, can he marry her sister? He said, 'Immediately if he wishes.'

And the ruling of the Mut'ah (temporary marriage) husband regarding the prohibition and combining of the two sisters is the same as the permanent (Batta) husband, because His Exalted Saying, 'And that you join together two sisters,' is general for all of that.
ai.seo_question: Can a man marry two sisters if his first wife dies or is divorced?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the distinction between *hadr* (prohibition due to concurrent marriage) and *jam'* (prohibition due to permanent exclusion) regarding sisters. It establishes that while divorce requires waiting for the *iddah* to clear the specific bond before marrying the sister, death permits immediate marriage, a ruling extended to *mut'ah* (temporary marriage) based on the generality of the Quranic verse. This highlights the Shia juristic principle that the prohibition of marrying two sisters is not absolute but conditional upon the timing of the marital bonds.
